2. The appellant / applicant has been convicted under Sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 (1) and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 by judgment dated 19.08.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge -VI-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Gopalganj in POCSO Case No.

3. The victim is a fourteen year old girl, who has alleged that the appellant had raped her.

Though there has been a delay in reporting the matter, but the victim has come out with an explanation,
namely, her being overcome by the fear of the appellant harming her parents.

sentences.text:
4. The mother of the victim, who has been examined as PW1, has alleged that sometimes in the past,
the appellant had committed rape on her too.

5. Mr. Ansul, the learned Advocate has read out a paragraph from deposition of PW1 to show that she has admitted that she was in a relationship with the appellant and when she fell out with the appellant, the instant case has been lodged.

Otherwise, there would have been no reason for the mother of the victim also to have withheld the information about her having Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1025 of 2023(3) dt.16-01-2024 been raped by the appellant in the past.
6.

In fact, the allegation in the F.I.R. is that the appellant had impressed upon the parents of the victim that they ought to change their residence as the neighbourhood in which they resided was not very safe.
On that pretext, the victim was taken on a motorcycle and the parents of the victim were asked to follow but before the parents of the victim could change their residence, the victim was raped.

7. Though, the learned Advocate for the appellant has tried to show that the entire story is cooked-up with an oblique motive, especially on account of delay in reporting of the case and the doctor not having found any injury on the genitalia of the victim even though she was only a fourteen year old girl; but regard being had to the nature of accusation against the appellant, we are not inclined to suspend his sentence during the pendency of the appeal, presently.
8. The prayer for suspension of sentence of the appellant is rejected.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1025 of 2023(3) dt.16-01-2024 9.
However, in accordance with the mandate of Section 374 (4) Cr.P.C., we direct the Registry of this Court to prepare the paper-book with urgent dispatch.

10. Let this appeal be listed for hearing within first ten cases, in the first week of March,
commencing from 4th of March, 2024.
(Ashutosh Kumar, J) ( Nani Tagia, J) sunilkumar/-
